stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( f(2) = 3 \), \( f(4) = -1 \), \( f(8) = 2 \). Let \( g(x) = \int_{x^{2}}^{x^{3}} f(t) \, dt \). Find the value of \( g'\left(2\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Split the integral at any constant k in the domain of the integrand: \( g(x) = \int_{k}^{x^{3}} f(t) \, dt - \int_{k}^{x^{2}} f(t) \, dt \), and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to each piece.
With the chain rule, \( g'(x) = f\left(x^{3}\right) \cdot 3 x^{2} - f\left(x^{2}\right) \cdot 2 x \).
At \( x = 2 \): the limits are \( 8 \) and \( 4 \), with derivatives \( 12 \) and \( 4 \), and \( f\left(8\right) = 2 \), \( f\left(4\right) = -1 \).

distractor_derivations.A: f(upper) - f(lower) with both chain rule factors left off
distractor_derivations.B: integrand evaluated at x = 2 instead of at the two limits
distractor_derivations.C: lower limit term added instead of subtracted
